definitions.explanation: a condition or assumption that must be accepted as the basis for an argument, plan, or action

examples.japanese: それを{前提|ぜんてい}に{話|はな}す。
{結婚|けっこん}を{前提|ぜんてい}に{付|つ}き{合|あ}う。
examples.english: To date with marriage in mind.

examples.japanese: この{計画|けいかく}は{全員|ぜんいん}{参加|さんか}を{前提|ぜんてい}としている。

notes:
USAGE:
- 〜を{前提|ぜんてい}に/として (on the premise of ~; assuming ~)
- {前提|ぜんてい}{条件|じょうけん} (precondition, prerequisite)
- {大|だい}{前提|ぜんてい} (major premise - in logic)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {結婚|けっこん}を{前提|ぜんてい}に (with marriage in mind - said of dating)
- {前提|ぜんてい}が{崩|くず}れる (the premise collapses)

LOGIC:
In formal logic: {大前提|だいぜんてい} (major premise), {小前提|しょうぜんてい} (minor premise)

RELATED WORDS:
- {仮定|かてい} (assumption, hypothesis)
- {条件|じょうけん} (condition)
- {基|もと} (basis)
